content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon, particularly after a sharp price drop or recovery.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price spikes — forecasts lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days.
- Tends to overshoot after a spike, then corrects with a downward bias in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring structural trends.
- Underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., below 65) and overestimates in high-price regimes (e.g., above 75).
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fails to capture sudden reversals or sharp directional changes in price.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent price movements are underweighted in forecasting, leading to persistent bias in mid-to-late horizon.
